youtube.title: Why your key is a PIN: how does a key open a lock? #shorts
youtube.description:
How does a key open a lock? Inside a normal door lock is a row of tiny pins (usually five), each cut in two and pushed down by a spring. Without a key, the top halves sit across the line where the lock turns, so it's jammed. Your key's bumps are all different heights: the right key lifts every pin so each split lands exactly on that line, and the lock turns. One bump a hair off and it's stuck. That's how locks work: a pin tumbler lock is basically a PIN code cut in metal, and the idea is roughly 4,000 years old.
